Learn to explain how an app talks to a test server and a live server: Production, Staging & Base URL, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Production - The live version of your backend and app that real users use every day.
Staging - A test copy of the live setup, where the team checks changes before real users see them.
Base URL - The first part of every web address your app calls, shared by all of its requests.

landscape.title: iOS Production, Staging & Base URL | Day 233
landscape.description:
Explain Production, Staging & Base URL in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Production, Staging, Base URL 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Production - The live version of your backend and app that real users use every day.
한국어: Production: 실제 사용자가 매일 쓰는 라이브 백엔드와 앱

Staging - A test copy of the live setup, where the team checks changes before real users see them.
한국어: Staging: 실제 사용자에게 보이기 전에 팀이 변경 사항을 확인하는 라이브 환경의 테스트 복사본

Base URL - The first part of every web address your app calls, shared by all of its requests.
한국어: Base URL: 앱이 호출하는 모든 요청이 공유하는 웹 주소의 앞부분

In this video, Mina and Jake talk about why a test build shows empty data and how the base URL picks a server, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Production, Staging and Base URL in English?

dialogue.title: Which server is this?
dialogue.setting: A test build shows empty data

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our test build shows empty data. Is the server down?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check the environment first. Your build probably points to staging.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A test copy of the live setup. The team checks changes there before users see them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And production is the real one?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, production is the live backend that real users use every day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So how does the app know which one to call?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Through the base URL. Every request starts with the base URL.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In our code, `env` picks the base URL, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. If `env` is `.staging`, we use the test host.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the empty data is just the staging database.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Staging is safe to break, but production is not a playground.

dialogue.code:
import Foundation
enum Env { case staging, production }
let env = Env.staging
let base = URL(string: env == .staging
    ? "https://stg.example.com"
    : "https://api.example.com")!
